# State Machine Design 🧩

#### Course: Brick Breaker with JavaScript

## State Machine Design 🧩

Four states controlled everything in this game:

```javascriptDOM
const STATE = Object.freeze({
  MENU:      "MENU",
  PLAYING:   "PLAYING",
  PAUSED:    "PAUSED",
  GAME_OVER: "GAME_OVER",
});
```

Two patterns kept it clean throughout.

Guard clauses made sure logic only ran in the right state:

```javascriptDOM
update() {
  if (this.state !== STATE.PLAYING) return;  // everything else ignored
  ...
}
```

Discrete transition handlers meant each user action had one responsible function:

```javascriptDOM
handleAdvance()     // click or space
handlePauseToggle() // P or Escape
```

No physics ran on the menu. No input was accepted during game over. No transition could fire twice from one keypress. Those are entire categories of bugs that never had a chance to exist.

You will see this same structure in React Router, in Unity, and in backend service orchestrators. You built it from scratch using a frozen object and a few if statements.
